doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Arriving in New York in 1963 on faith
summary: He knew no one, went to jam sessions, and word spread; he went on the road with singers and then Rahsaan Roland Kirk, Max Roach, Art Blakey and eventually Miles.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The spirits are with us. Well most of your generation seems like New York beckoned. Did you feel prepared when you went there in 1963 or did you just have faith?

Oh, that’s it. In my case I definitely had faith. Because I didn’t know anything about New York City and so it was just faith. I didn’t know anyone and so you just start going around to jam sessions. I remember I caught the tail end of Birdland, you know, the real Birdland I guess, right here on Broad Street. Broadway — I’m thinking of Richmond — Broadway, and you’d go down in the basement and so you know you’d listen and I think one night I tried to sit in but I didn’t know, I just climbed on stage and so but that’s a good way of putting it. In my case it was just pure faith.
Did you have to work a day job, like to get by?

No because you do a lot of jobs as sideman and then what happens certain people hear you and start spreading your name around. And they said, “Oh man, we’ve got this new kid in town, plays piano, he sounds pretty good.” Then you start getting calls. I think — oh in the beginning I went on the road with a lot of singers, you know, Betty Carter — for some reason Betty Carter always knew the new pianists when they came in town, and there was the Dakota Staton, Al Hibbler, Joe Williams, and then, you know I got a call from Rahsaan Roland Kirk and was there for a while. And then the next thing I think was Max Roach. I was with Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers for a while, and Chuck Mangione was playing trumpet in the group. So you just keep building like that then eventually you get a call from Miles.
